correctness.rationale: The proof reduces isometrically to \(\mathcal L(\ell_{p'}^2,\ell_q^2)\), uses exact endpoint norms of the two-point Walsh--Hadamard transform, interpolates with \(\theta=2/p\), and applies the exact two-dimensional norm-comparison factor. The normalized transform \(A\) and reflected copy \(B\) both have norm \(1\), while \(\|A+B\|=\|A-B\|=2\) is attained on coordinate vectors. The universal upper bound \(C_{\mathrm{NJ}}\le2\) then gives equality. Boundary cases \(p=2\), \(p=\infty\), and \(q=\infty\) are included by the same formulas and the convention \(1/\infty=0\).

value.rationale: The focal paper leaves a natural finite-dimensional injective parameter gap between its reciprocal-sum region and the general operator-space criterion. The accepted statement fills a large, geometrically natural portion of that gap: every parameter pair with at least one exponent at least \(2\), including the entire boundary lines \(p=2\) or \(q=2\). It reduces the unresolved classical finite-dimensional injective plane to \(1\le p,q<2\) and does so with a reusable explicit Walsh--Hadamard witness rather than a routine restatement.
